key_insight: A single deep model jointly predicts bioactivity and reconstructs molecules while providing a principled measure of distribution shift, enabling reliable detection of out-of-distribution chemistry. Experimentally validated: the approach led to discovery of active inhibitors for two clinically relevant kinases.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of making molecular ML models reliable on novel regions of chemical space by quantifying when predictions are out-of-distribution and prioritizing candidates that are both predicted active and within the model's trusted domain.
method: Train a multitask model that simultaneously learns to predict bioactivity and reconstruct molecular structures (encoder–decoder + predictor integrated objective).
Derive a principled distribution-shift/uncertainty metric from the model’s internal representations to flag out-of-distribution inputs.
Validate end-to-end by selecting high-confidence candidates and experimentally testing them, discovering active inhibitors for two kinase targets.
impact: Provides a practical way for ML practitioners to assess and mitigate out-of-distribution risk in molecular prediction tasks, improving trustworthiness and accelerating the pipeline from in silico hits to experimental validation.

paper_title: Molecular deep learning at the edge of chemical space
paper_authors: Derek van Tilborg, Luke Rossen, Francesca Grisoni
